description: Deterministic symptom-cause-fix knowledge for grounded Niagara planning and refinement.

entries.title: Collision does not spawn a secondary effect
causes: Collision resets or changes particle velocity before the event velocity threshold is evaluated.
The event generator or receiver is placed in the wrong script usage or event handler.
The receiver emitter, renderer, or event handler is disabled.
The source emitter is using GPU simulation while the selected event route requires CPU support.
fixes: Inspect module order and the collision-event threshold before changing spawn rate or scale.
Inspect source and receiver emitter enabled state, Persistent IDs, exact event-generator name, and event-handler configuration.
Preserve pre-collision velocity or use a compatible trigger condition.
Keep unrelated visibility and scale adjustments in separate objectives so they can roll back independently.
entries.evidence_scope: historical UE56 diagnosis hypothesis; not independently validated in UE58

entries.title: Event data overwrites the intended spawn location
patterns: secondary particles spawn at the wrong position
causes: Event payload position is applied after Shape Location and overwrites the earlier position.
The event receiver is bound to the wrong source emitter or event payload attribute.
A later Set Variables module overwrites Particles.Position.
fixes: Inspect parameter-map order and identify the final writer of Particles.Position.
Use event position as the base and apply the desired local offset afterward.
Verify source-emitter and event-payload bindings before adjusting random shape parameters.
entries.evidence_scope: historical UE56 diagnosis hypothesis; not independently validated in UE58

entries.title: Camera-following particles trail behind or refill slowly
patterns: weather field refills after camera movement
카메라 이동 후 파티클이 다시 채워짐
causes: The emitter is in world space, so existing particles remain at their old world positions when the component moves.
The spawn volume is too small or particle lifetime is too long for a camera-following field.
A camera offset moves the component outside the reviewed view while the effect itself remains healthy.
fixes: Inspect local-space state before increasing spawn rate.
For camera-following weather, prefer local space and a bounded spawn volume sized to the view.
Review lifetime, spawn volume, and camera offset together; keep density tuning as a separate objective.

entries.title: Effect is invisible without its source runtime controller
patterns: works only with the original weather actor
causes: A source weather/controller actor normally supplies user parameters, arrays, textures, or kill volumes.
A copied emitter still references source materials, Niagara parameter collections, scripts, or data interfaces.
A visibility or kill module treats missing user data as a condition that removes every particle.
fixes: Inspect user parameters, data-interface overrides, and dependency audit before changing visual values.
Recreate the required behavior with project-owned or engine assets and stable defaults.
Run promotion audit and plugin/source-independence checks before treating the effect as durable content.

entries.title: Particles compile but are not visible
causes: Spawn rate, lifetime, scale, or alpha is zero or effectively zero.
The emitter or renderer is disabled, or the renderer has no usable material.
Fixed bounds cull the particles, especially for GPU simulation.
A material, texture, or source dependency is missing.
fixes: Inspect compile state, enabled state, spawn/lifetime values, renderer material, and bounds in that order.
Capture runtime particle counts before compensating with larger scale or spawn rate.
Separate logic restoration from aesthetic tuning so visibility compensations can roll back.

entries.title: GPU particles are clipped or disappear because of bounds
causes: GPU simulation uses fixed bounds that do not cover the authored motion volume.
Bounds were copied from a template with a different coordinate scale or local-space policy.
The component moves while world-space particles extend beyond the fixed box.
fixes: Inspect sim target, local space, and fixed bounds as one contract.
Size bounds from the intended spawn and motion envelope, then re-run visual review.
Avoid using an oversized bounds change to mask a world/local-space design error.

entries.title: Rain sprites look like blobs instead of velocity-aligned streaks
patterns: sprites do not align to velocity
causes: Sprite Size Mode is uniform instead of non-uniform.
Sprite renderer alignment is not VelocityAligned.
Velocity or sprite rotation conflicts with the intended streak direction.
fixes: Inspect the Initialize Particle static switch and Sprite Size input.
Use velocity-aligned sprite rendering for directional streaks.
Tune width, length, velocity, and material silhouette as separate objectives.

entries.title: Particles spawn on the wrong axis or in the wrong volume
patterns: particles spread vertically instead of horizontally
causes: Shape Location dimensions or axis masks do not match the intended world/local orientation.
Velocity direction is being mistaken for spawn-distribution direction.
The emitter local-space setting changes how the authored axis is interpreted.
fixes: Inspect Shape Location inputs and emitter local-space state together.
Separate spawn-volume correction from velocity correction.
Use a deterministic preview camera and compare spatial coverage before and after the patch.

entries.title: Compile failure after module or static-switch edits
causes: A static switch activates inputs that have incompatible or missing overrides.
A literal or RapidIteration value does not match the resolved Niagara input type.
GPU simulation is incompatible with a selected module or data interface.
A stale module selector targeted a different stack function after graph changes.
fixes: Inspect current static-switch options and module-input candidates before writing.
Use node GUID or exact module selectors and stale-value guards where available.
Compile and inspect after each objective; roll back the objective that introduced the error.

entries.title: Repeated tuning accumulates compensating parameter drift
patterns: scale became too large after iterations
causes: Visibility symptoms were compensated with spawn rate or scale before the underlying logic error was fixed.
Multiple unrelated changes were grouped into one patch and could not be rolled back selectively.
The latest state was accepted even though an earlier iteration scored better.
fixes: Group operations by explicit visual objective and expected observation.
Roll back only failed objectives while preserving independently successful objectives.
Store every scored state and select the best historical state rather than the final iteration.
